To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following factors contribute to the translation of equitable access into retention, success, and completion in marginalized groups in higher education: (a) the development of a holistic, integrated, and student-centered approach to the provision of academic and non-academic student support, (b) the provision of student support that is responsive to the needs of the individual student, and (c) the provision of a student-centered approach to student support that includes the development of a student support plan.

the following strategies facilitate the translation of equitable access into retention of students in marginalized groups in higher education: (a) student selection using tools predictive and diagnostic of student success, (b) comprehensive and holistic student and staff support, and (c) curriculum and pedagogic interventions that are responsive to the needs of marginalized groups.
